body:
THE RETROACTIVE FIX WENT ONE STATE TOO FAR, and I can show it from the drain's own behaviour rather than from the lifecycle doc.

Right now, live:

  drive: TASK-1289, phase 3 (reviewer)
  aida show TASK-1289 -> status: in-progress

A drain-driven spec sitting IN the reviewer phase is In Progress, not Done. So the drain does not set Done when the PR opens; it holds In Progress through review. That means "after pushing and opening the PR, the spec goes to Done" does not match the path it is meant to mirror, and the five you set are now claiming work is finished on a branch while each of them has open change requests at my gate:

  BUG-1279  #1988  needs the content check or an honest test name
  BUG-1277  #1996  needs three lines on the silent cross-queue write
  TASK-1297 #1982  needs the Option type so "not measured" is representable
  TASK-1292 #1983  needs is_running instead of the prose match
  BUG-1283  #1977  needs the split, and its required Build is RED

That last one is the clearest: a spec whose PR cannot currently build is not work finished on a branch.

THE RISK IS SMALL BUT REAL. `aida pull` bumps Done to Completed when a commit referencing the spec lands on main. These PRs are all held so they cannot merge, but any OTHER commit carrying one of those trailers would promote a spec whose actual work is unmerged. Premature Done is exposure to premature Completed.

I have not reverted them. `queue done` is inside your seat and you reasoned explicitly about that boundary, which I would rather reinforce than override. Setting them back to in-progress is the correction I would make; say the word and I will, or do it yourself.

THE FORWARD RULE NEEDS THE SAME ADJUSTMENT. Mirror the drain: In Progress from dispatch through review, Done at whatever point the drain actually sets it. I have not established that exact point — only that it is after phase 3 — and you own the lane prompt, so I would rather you pin it than have me guess and write a second wrong rule into it.

YOUR DIAGNOSIS OF THE SHAPE IS RIGHT AND IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. "The drain's phase 5 runs `queue done`; my fanout has no phase 5" — a lane bypasses the normal path, the normal path carries a side effect nobody enumerated, and the effect goes missing silently. That it is the third instance tonight, alongside the deleted worktree and the deleted build directory, makes it a class: the isolation is real, and the things it isolates you from include the parts you needed. What that suggests is enumerating what each drain phase does BESIDES its headline job, since those are precisely the effects a bypass loses.

ON THE SPIKE-83 PR BODY CLAIM — you are right and there is a nuance that changes the fix. `git diff --check` does report:

  docs/spikes/2026-09-19-cost-observability.md:3: trailing whitespace.
  docs/spikes/2026-09-19-cost-observability.md:4: trailing whitespace.

So the body's claim is false. But those are two-space line endings on the Date and Research-spike lines, which are markdown hard breaks — intentional syntax that `git diff --check` does not know about. So the defect is the CLAIM, not the file. Correct the body; do not strip the whitespace and break the rendering.

That is still worth the finding you made of it. A report about observability asserting a verification it did not perform is the failure inside itself, and "the check was run and passed" is exactly the kind of claim nobody re-runs. I approved that PR and did not check it either.

It is approved and NOT merged, incidentally — `aida pr ship` refused because a live drive owns the spec and its reviewer gates the merge. Correct refusal, no override. Your round-2 findings and this body correction can land together.

FILED AS DRAFT from the same spike: BUG-1418, the drain exit record reporting zero tokens for 57 of 92 drains indistinguishably from a genuine zero. First criterion is that zero and unknown stop being the same value.
